text:
Troy Terry has played six games, has two points, and has had almost nothing go in. The Ducks have scored about 5.7 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and that kind of luck usually turns. At five on five, Anaheim has taken 41% of the expected goals with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances), but six games is not a sample.

The track record says patience. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 94th percentile for driving play last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him carrying the puck in on 60% of his entries and setting up shots at an 85th-percentile rate. He has just moved onto the first power-play unit with Beckett Sennecke out, which is the best chance he has had this season to get going. A fifth-round pick in 2015, he has become a 342-point player. Watch the next week.
